canonical_topic: Oil trap and related rock properties
definition: A trap is an impermeable rock layer sitting above a porous, permeable rock layer, which allows oil/gas to accumulate rather than escape; porosity and permeability describe how much fluid a rock can hold and how easily it can move through it.
core_idea: Oil accumulates where a permeable, porous reservoir rock is sealed beneath an impermeable cap rock (the trap); porosity measures storage capacity while permeability measures how connected/flowable that storage is.
key_points: Trap: impermeable rock layer located above a porous, permeable rock layer.
Porosity: ratio of empty (pore) space in a rock to the rock's total volume.
Permeability: how easily liquid/gas passes through rock, driven by how connected the pores are.
A rock can be highly porous yet impermeable if its pores are not interconnected.
Associated gas: natural gas produced from the same well as oil.
relationships: Porosity and permeability together determine whether a rock layer can serve as an oil reservoir beneath a trap
caveats: High porosity does not imply high permeability — a porous rock can still be impermeable if pores are disconnected.
